title: Dinner (cont.): one short plump banana, deeply ripe with brown speckling and streaking across most of the skin, unpeeled on the floral placemat. CARD AND FRUIT SHARE THE PLACEMAT, the good geometry, so this is a point estimate rather than the range a cross-frame reference would force. THE CARD IS NOTICEABLY FORESHORTENED HERE AND THE MAX RULE DOES REAL WORK: it images about 364 px on its long edge against roughly 250 px on its short, an apparent aspect near 1.44 against the true 1.586, so the long axis is the compressed one and the honest scale is the short edge at about 4.63 px/mm, NOT the 4.25 the long edge would have given — taking the long edge would have inflated every linear dimension by 9 percent and the derived volume by about 30 percent. The banana lies farther up frame than the card and therefore farther from the lens, so its own scale is a little lower again. THE FRUIT IS SHORT AND FAT RATHER THAN LONG: about 125mm from tip to stem and about 45mm through at the thickest, where a standard Cavendish runs 180 to 200mm long by 35mm, so this is either an apple or manzano type or simply a stubby one, and ITS SHAPE IS WHY LENGTH ALONE WOULD MISLEAD — by length it would read as an extra-small banana at 81g of flesh, by volume it is fatter than that. Treating it as a tapered near-elliptical cylinder at roughly 75 percent cross-section fill gives about 110ml, so near 103g whole with the peel and ABOUT 75g OF EDIBLE FLESH once the peel is off at its usual third of the weight. At USDA banana figures of 22.8g carbohydrate, 1.1g protein and 89 calories per 100g that is 17g of carbohydrate, 1g of protein and about 70 calories. THE RIPENESS IS A REAL VARIABLE AND IS RECORDED RATHER THAN IGNORED: heavy brown speckling means most of the resistant starch has already converted to free sugars, so the same grams arrive faster than they would from a green-tipped banana, though the total is unchanged. A small brown object lies on the mat to the right of the stem; it is not iden…

Dinner (cont.): FLOUNDER AND MUSSELS COOKED BY JAVIER, her words, served in a thick tomato sauce in a wide white soup plate with fried potato cubes banked at one side and five carrot batons laid across the rim. THIS IS THE PROTEIN COURSE FLAGGED AS MISSING AT 18:39 AND IT ARRIVED. NO SCALE REFERENCE IN FRAME, no SPG card, so the plate is the only ruler and it is an assumed one: the rim images 910 px across by 917 px top to bottom, essentially circular, WHICH MEANS THIS IS A NEAR TOP-DOWN FRAME at only a few degrees off vertical. That is the good case for footprint and the BAD case for height, so every depth below is an assumption and is labelled as one. Taking the plate as a 24cm soup plate gives 3.79 px/mm, and that assumption is CROSS-CHECKED BY THE MUSSELS: the lower mussel lies with both halves splayed flat and spans 370 px or 98mm across the pair, so about 49mm per shell, and the upper shell measures 239 px or 63mm — both squarely in the normal 5 to 7cm range for a blue mussel, which would not hold if the plate were a 20cm or a 28cm one. COMPONENT BUILD: three mussel meats are visible and countable at roughly 12g each for about 36g, WITH THE EXPLICIT CAVEAT THAT A HEAVY SAUCE CAN HIDE MORE and this count is of what the frame shows rather than of what was cooked. Flounder reads as three sauce-covered chunks near 5 by 3cm, thickness NOT measurable in a top-down frame and assumed at 2cm, giving roughly 110g of cooked fish. Fried potato cubes measure 16 to 21mm per cube across a 92 by 69mm bank in a loose single layer, about sixteen cubes at 5g, so roughly 80g, and they are read as potato from the golden crust and pale interior. Five carrot batons at about 95mm long by 12mm, roughly 40g. Tomato sauce depth is the softest figure of all for the same top-down reason, taken at about 100g. THAT GIVES 31g CARBOHYDRATE, 32g PROTEIN AND ABOUT 385 CALORIES FOR THIS COURSE, with the potatoes carrying half the carbohydrate and the fish and mussels carrying nearly all the pro…

Dinner (cont.): a stemmed glass of deep golden SPARKLING WHITE WINE, poured generously, standing on the glass patio table with a dark bottle behind it at the right of frame. IDENTIFICATION BASIS STATED SO SHE CAN CONTRADICT IT IN ONE WORD: fine bubbles are streaming continuously up the bowl in several distinct trains, which is a carbonated wine rather than a still one, and the colour is a deep gold rather than the pale straw of a young prosecco, so this is read as a cava or a similarly aged sparkling. A non-alcoholic sparkling cider would look much the same in a photograph, and if that is what it is the alcohol caution below does not apply and the carbs roughly quadruple, so this is the one line worth checking. NO SCALE REFERENCE IN FRAME and no card, so the volume comes from standard glassware proportions rather than measurement: the bowl is filled to about its widest point, which in an ordinary white wine glass is a generous pour near 175ml or 6oz rather than a standard 150ml. AT BRUT SPARKLING FIGURES the carbohydrate is only about 1 to 2g per 100ml, so ROUGHLY 3g OF CARBOHYDRATE, no protein, and about 130 calories of which nearly all is the ethanol itself at roughly 17g. CUMULATIVE WITH THE 18:39 OYSTERS, three minutes earlier, so the preBG anchor stays the FIRST item's 95 mg/dL and the carbs are summed for the Model v5 recomputation. THE CLINICALLY IMPORTANT POINT IS NOT THE CARBOHYDRATE, IT IS THE OVERNIGHT DIRECTION: ethanol suppresses hepatic gluconeogenesis for several hours after drinking, and tonight it lands on a dinner that so far carries 6g of carbohydrate from oysters and 12g of protein, with the whole day already light on protein at about 40g. That combination — alcohol, a very low carbohydrate evening and a 95 mg/dL starting point — is the recognised setup for a delayed nocturnal fall rather than for a spike. NOTED FOR THE ALERTING PATH: the overnight glucose alert threshold between 00:00 and 08:30 is BG below 70 only, so a soft drift into the low …

Dinner: SEVEN raw oysters on the half shell, plump and served in their own liquor with no sauce on the plate, on a white dinner plate with red and black rim bands, a lemon wedge and a fork beside it on the placemat. THE COUNT IS SEVEN AND IT IS TAKEN FROM THE FRAME, WHICH IS THE CORRECT PROCEDURE HERE AND IS WORTH SPELLING OUT AFTER YESTERDAY. On 2026-08-14 an oyster course was logged as six because she SAID six, and she later clarified that six was her PLAN for the course while the frame honestly showed the three then on the plate. Today there is NO CAPTION AND NO STATED COUNT, so her standing rule of 2026-08-13 governs — fully in frame means intended and counted — and the shells are individually separable rather than heaped, each with its own visible meat, so seven is a direct count and not an estimate off a pile. NO SCALE REFERENCE IN FRAME: the SPG card is absent, so the plate is the only ruler and it is an assumed one. The plate ellipse runs about 1160 px across by 870 px deep, giving cos theta near 0.75 and a viewing angle around 41 degrees, and taking it as a standard 26cm dinner plate yields roughly 4.46 px/mm. On that scale the shells measure about 100mm along their long axes once the depth axis is corrected by cos theta, which is a good-sized oyster rather than a small one. MEAT WEIGHT IS THE SOFT NUMBER AND IT IS ANCHORED TO THE 2026-08-14 OYSTER COURSE FOR CONSISTENCY rather than re-derived, at about 18g of meat per shell, so SEVEN OYSTERS IS ROUGHLY 126g OF OYSTER MEAT. At Pacific oyster figures near 81 calories, 4.9g carbohydrate, 9.5g protein and 2.3g fat per 100g, that is about 6g of carbohydrate, 12g of protein and 100 calories. IF THE PLATE ASSUMPTION IS WRONG THE ERROR IS PROPORTIONAL and would move meat weight by the cube of it, which is the price of no card — worth noting only because oysters are so low in carbohydrate that even a large error here barely moves the projection. NOT CUMULATIVE: the previous food was the 16:57 apple half, 1 hour 42…

Snack: half a red-skinned apple, cut face up on the floral placemat with the core and two pips visible, skin left on. CLASSIFIED SNACK ON THE HOUR TABLE: 16:57 sits in the 16:00 to 17:59 Snack band. NOT CUMULATIVE — the previous food was the 14:06 cherries, 2 hours 51 minutes earlier, so the live 113 mg/dL is the honest preBG rather than a mid-digestion reading. CARD AND APPLE SHARE THE PLACEMAT, the good geometry, but TWO OPPOSING CORRECTIONS APPLY HERE AND THEY VERY NEARLY CANCEL, which is worth writing out because taking either one alone would have been wrong in a different direction. The card images about 367 px on its long edge by 225 px on its short, an apparent aspect of 1.63 against the true 1.586, giving 4.29 px/mm at the card's own position. The apple's cut face spans about 322 px across frame, the across-frame axis that needs no depth correction, which is a naive 75mm. FIRST CORRECTION, DOWNWARD: the cut face is not on the mat, it is the top of a half apple lying dome-down, some 40mm above the card's plane and therefore nearer the lens, which at a 40cm working distance images it about 10 percent large. SECOND CORRECTION, UPWARD: the apple sits roughly 500 px higher in the frame than the card, which in a tilted shot is farther from the lens by perhaps 6cm, imaging it about 13 percent small. Net effect is close to unity and THE CUT FACE IS ABOUT 75mm, a standard USDA medium apple, whose whole weight is 182g, so THE HALF IS ABOUT 90g GROSS AND 82g OF EDIBLE FLESH ONCE THE CORE IS OFF, giving 11g of carbohydrate, 0.2g of protein and about 45 calories. CROSS-CHECKED AGAINST THE 2026-08-14 15:05 APPLE HALF AND THEY GENUINELY DIFFER: that cut face measured 60mm against today's 75mm, so today's apple is materially the larger fruit and the difference is real rather than method drift. ONE FLAG ON THAT OLDER ROW WITHOUT REWRITING IT: it derived 130g for a 60mm whole apple, where the USDA figures imply nearer 90g at that diameter, so its 65g half was generous and to…

Lunch (cont.): SEVEN dark sweet cherries with stems attached, laid out individually on the floral placemat rather than heaped. THE ARRANGEMENT IS THE STORY OF THIS ENTRY AND IT SOLVES YESTERDAY'S PROBLEM: on 2026-08-14 a piled cluster was counted as eight and Maria corrected it to six, the lesson being that overlapping glossy fruit distorts a count in BOTH directions. Here every cherry is physically separate with mat visible between them, so the count is direct observation rather than an estimate off a heap, and SEVEN is stated with confidence. THE CARD LIES ON THE SAME PLACEMAT AS THE FRUIT, which per the 2026-08-13 plum lesson is the good geometry: reference and food share a plane, so this is a point estimate rather than the range a distant reference would force. Card measures roughly 400 px on the long edge by 255 px on the short, an apparent aspect of 1.57 against the true 1.586, so it is essentially square-on to the lens and this is a near top-down frame, giving 4.72 px/mm at the card's own position low in the frame. The cherries sit higher in frame and therefore farther from the lens, so their scale is nearer 4.3 to 4.5 px/mm; their measured widths run 110 to 130 px with a mean of about 119, which resolves to ROUGHLY 26 TO 27mm PER CHERRY, a good-sized sweet cherry rather than an average one. Taken as slightly flattened spheres near 8.5ml each that is about 9g with the pit and 8g of flesh, so SEVEN CHERRIES IS ABOUT 60g WITH PITS AND 56g EDIBLE, giving 9g of carbohydrate, 0.6g of protein and 35 calories at the USDA sweet-cherry figures of 16g carb and 63 calories per 100g. CUMULATIVE WITH THE 13:52 LUNCH, 14 MINUTES EARLIER AND WELL INSIDE THE HOUR, so the preBG anchor is the FIRST item's 84 mg/dL and NOT the live 93 mg/dL now showing, which is already mid-digestion and would inflate the projection. Carbs summed across both plates for the Model v5 recomputation. [Cumulative Lunch: 49g carbs total] (BG: 84 mg/dL Flat) (Pred: 129-149 mg/dL @ 3:16 PM) (Protein: …

Lunch: a mezze plate on her small yellow-rimmed ICE CREAM dessert plate — raw broccoli florets, a large double scoop of hummus with an orange-tinted second flavour spooned over one side, a pile of thin dark purple beet chips, and a fan of pale seeded crackers. SCALE REFERENCE IS THE SPG CARD AT 85.6mm BUT IT LIES ON THE PLACEMAT, NOT ON THE PLATE, so it does not share the food's plane and every figure here is an estimate with a plane correction applied rather than a direct reading. Card measures about 323 px on the long edge by 208 px on the short, an apparent aspect of 1.55 against the true 1.586, so it is very nearly square-on to the lens and gives about 3.85 px/mm at its own position on the mat. The plate ellipse runs 680 px across by 485 px deep, so cos theta is about 0.713 and THE VIEWING ANGLE IS ROUGHLY 44 DEGREES, at the steep end of the useful band and therefore good for reading height off the side of the hummus. The plate sits farther from the lens than the card, so about 3.5 px/mm at the food, which scales the plate to roughly 19 to 20cm and confirms it is a dessert plate rather than a dinner plate — worth stating because the same pile on a 26cm plate would have been read as half again as much food. PER COMPONENT: hummus footprint about 8.5cm with its front edge standing roughly 65 px proud of the plate, which at sin theta 0.70 is a measured 2.6cm of height rather than an assumed dome, giving a spherical cap near 78ml, and about 67ml after the 0.857 volume correction for the food sitting some 2cm above the card's plane, so ROUGHLY 70g OR A QUARTER CUP of hummus. Broccoli florets about 3cm per head across roughly six heads in a single layer, about 90g or a cup of florets. Beet chips are thin and airy and their pile volume badly overstates their mass, per the 2026-08-14 bowl lesson, so they are carried at about 18g rather than by volume. Seven seeded crackers at about 4cm each, roughly 22g. A single white oblong tablet also lies on the placemat and is not …

Breakfast: one fried egg, sunny side up with the yolk whole and a heavy grind of black pepper over it, plus an open-faced slice of her own homemade whole grain multi-seed bread with jamon serrano draped over it in folded slices. THE SCALE REFERENCE IS THE SPG CARD AT 85.6mm BUT IT IS LYING ON THE PLACEMAT, NOT ON THE PLATE, so it does not share the food's plane and this entry is a range rather than a point estimate, per the 2026-08-13 plum lesson. Card measures roughly 300 px on the long edge and 200 px on the short, giving about 3.7 px/mm at the card's own position; the plate ellipse cross-checks it at 865 px across by 675 px deep, so cos theta about 0.78 and a viewing angle near 39 degrees, which is squarely in the useful 30-45 range. Correcting the card scale for the plate being farther from the lens and the food sitting about 2cm above the mat gives about 3.6 px/mm at the food, so the plate is roughly 24cm and the egg white about 13.5cm across, one large fried egg at roughly 55g cooked in a little oil. THE BREAD IS NOT RE-MEASURED FROM THE PHOTO: it is one slice of her known 9x5 loaf and is carried at the standing 45g and 18g of carbs per the loaf calibration, which outranks any pixel estimate of a slice partly hidden under ham. The ham covers the full slice and ruffles over its far edge in what reads as two or three very thin slices, estimated at about 35g of serrano, the least certain number here since drape hides layers. A single white oblong tablet also sits on the plate rim and is not food, so it carries no macros and no Medication row is written from it. (BG: 94 mg/dL Flat) (Pred: 135-155 mg/dL @ 11:44 AM) (Protein: 22g | Carbs: ~19g | Cals: ~320) [Coach: Egg and ham put about 22g of protein on the plate before noon, and with a single slice of your bread the carbs stay down at 19g. Starting from 94, that is a gentle morning. Some sliced tomato or peppers alongside would round it right out.]

Dinner (dessert course): four dark-chocolate-covered cashews, one of them already bitten into and showing the whole cashew inside, with a small pile of dark sweet cherries on their stems, PLUS THREE STRAWBERRIES THAT ARE NOT IN THE PHOTO. Her words at 20:34 were add three strawberries to the picture, which is her supplying an item the frame does not contain, the mirror image of the six-oyster count at 19:01 where the frame under-showed what was served. TWO COUNTS HERE HAVE DIFFERENT CONFIDENCE AND THE DIFFERENCE IS STATED RATHER THAN GLOSSED. The strawberries and the chocolate cashews are solid: she stated three strawberries outright, and the four cashews are individually separated on the towel with clear space between them, so nothing can hide. THE CHERRIES ARE THE WEAK COUNT AT ABOUT EIGHT VISIBLE, because they are PILED IN A CLUSTER rather than laid out flat and the lower layer can conceal fruit, which is precisely the failure the oysters demonstrated ninety minutes ago when only three of six were in frame. The count is therefore recorded as eight to ten with eight used, worth about 2g of carbohydrate across that spread. NO SCALE REFERENCE IN FRAME and none needed, since every item here is a countable unit of well-known size rather than a portion of bulk food, which is the easiest measurement case there is. Build: four chocolate-covered cashews at roughly 4g each, a whole cashew being about 1.4g and the dark chocolate shell carrying the rest, so about 16g total giving 7g carbohydrate, 2g protein and 85 calories; eight sweet cherries at roughly 8g gross each, about 58g of flesh once the pits are out, giving 9g carbohydrate and 37 calories; three medium strawberries at roughly 12g each for 36g, giving 3g carbohydrate and 12 calories. THE FRUIT IS TWO THIRDS OF THE CARBOHYDRATE AND ONE THIRD OF THE CALORIES, the chocolate the reverse, which is the right way round for a dessert. NOT CUMULATIVE: the 19:12 chicken course was 1 hour 22 minutes earlier, outside the 1-ho…

Dinner (cont.): a large piece of roast chicken with glossy browned skin, bone underneath, served on a plate with one slice of her own homemade whole grain multi-seed bread. This is the second course she signalled at 19:01. THE SCALE REFERENCE HERE IS THE BREAD, NOT THE CARD, AND THAT CHOICE IS THE WHOLE POINT OF THIS ENTRY. The SPG card sits at the bottom-left of the frame on the placemat, nearest the lens, and gives 4.73 px/mm; applying that to the plate would make the plate 182mm, which is plainly too small and is the same near-foreground inflation that produced the 2x plum error on 2026-08-13 and the turkey-sized drumsticks at 15:05 today. THE BREAD SLICE SOLVES IT BECAUSE ITS TRUE SIZE IS NOW KNOWN INDEPENDENTLY AND IT LIES IN THE FOOD'S OWN PLANE: from the 18-slice loaf count its face is the pan cross-section at about 11.5cm across, it images at about 470px, so the plate plane runs at ABOUT 4.09 px/mm. That figure then makes the plate 210mm, a 21cm plate, which matches the 22cm plate measured at lunch today from an entirely separate photo — TWO INDEPENDENT ROUTES AGREEING, and the first time a known food item rather than the card has carried the calibration. THE GENERAL RULE WORTH KEEPING: an object of known size sitting in the food's own plane beats a more precisely known object sitting in a different plane. The chicken images at about 470px across by 380px deep; the plate's ellipse at 700 against 860px puts the view near 36 degrees off vertical, so dividing the depth axis by cos 36 gives a footprint of roughly 115 by 115mm. Height is the weak term as always, read as about 5cm of dome, and treating the piece as a partial half-ellipsoid at roughly 55 percent fill gives about 190ml, or ABOUT 200g gross and roughly 150g of meat and skin once the bone beneath is deducted, with an honest range of 120 to 180g. A roasted breast half with skin runs 150 to 200g, so the food-size prior agrees with the pixels here rather than contradicting them. BREAD TAKEN STRAIGHT FRO…

Dinner (first course): six raw oysters on the half shell with a pool of red cocktail sauce for dipping, served on a slate alongside a blue bowl of sauteed dark leafy greens tossed with shredded carrot. She flagged this explicitly as a FIRST COURSE, so a second course is expected and, if it lands inside the hour, will be logged as a cumulative continuation anchored on THIS entry's preBG of 94 rather than on the live reading at that time. COUNT STATED BY MARIA AT SIX, and only three oysters are visible in frame, which is the entire reason the count matters: a photo-derived count would have been WRONG BY HALF here and no amount of measurement care would have caught it. Her stated count is used verbatim, exactly as her 1.5 cups, her 8oz bowl and her 18 slices were earlier. NO SCALE REFERENCE IN FRAME — no SPG card, and the blue bowl is not the 237ml one already anchored — so nothing here is measured against a known object and PORTIONS COME FROM STANDARD SIZES RATHER THAN FROM GEOMETRY, which is stated plainly rather than dressed up as a measurement. The shells read as medium-to-large Pacific oysters at roughly 8 to 9cm, yielding ABOUT 18g of meat each or roughly 110g total, with an honest range of 90 to 130g. Macros at USDA Pacific oyster values of 81 calories, 9.45g protein and 4.95g carbohydrate per 100g; note oysters DO carry carbohydrate as glycogen, about 5g here, which is easy to forget on a food that reads as pure protein. Cocktail sauce taken at roughly 2 tablespoons for about 6g carbohydrate and 25 calories, that being ketchup-based and the single sweetest item on the plate. Greens estimated at roughly a cup cooked, about 120g of leaves plus 35g of shredded carrot, with a couple of teaspoons of cooking oil, giving about 8g carbohydrate, 4g protein and 125 calories. THE GREENS ARE COUNTED because they are fully in frame, per her own rule of 2026-08-13 that full framing signals intent. Recorded without comment to her: dark leafy greens at dinner run against her …

Lunch: two roast poultry drumsticks with crisp browned skin and pale torn meat still attached, served on a plate, with a thick slice of her own homemade whole grain multi-seed bread and half an apple cut face up alongside on the placemat. All three items are FULLY IN FRAME and are therefore all counted, per her stated rule of 2026-08-13 that full framing means intent and only something sneaking into a corner is accidental. TWO DIFFERENT GEOMETRIES IN ONE SHOT AND THEY DESERVE DIFFERENT CONFIDENCE. The bread and the apple sit on the placemat WITH the SPG card, same plane, so they are measured by direct ratio against the card and are the trustworthy half: the card images with a long axis of about 271px, the bread at about 380px long by 190px tall giving roughly 120 by 60mm, near enough identical to the 123 by 71mm slice measured this morning off the same loaf, so it is taken as the SAME SLICE SIZE at about 50g. The apple half spans about 205px across frame giving roughly 65mm at the mat plane, about 60mm after correcting for its own 35mm centre height, so a whole apple of about 130g and A HALF AT ABOUT 65g. THE CHICKEN IS THE WEAK HALF AND IS DELIBERATELY GIVEN A RANGE RATHER THAN A POINT VALUE: it sits on an ELEVATED PLATE, a different plane from the card, which is exactly the arrangement that produced the 2x plum error on 2026-08-13, so no point estimate is warranted. The plate reads about 737px across, or 233mm at the mat plane and roughly 222mm after plane correction. The left drumstick spans about 552px, which is 2.04 times the card's long axis and therefore ABOUT 174mm at the mat plane or 159mm corrected — LONG FOR CHICKEN AND MORE TYPICAL OF TURKEY, and the possibility that these are turkey drumsticks rather than chicken is left open here because the macros barely differ, roughly 216 versus 208 calories and 27 versus 28g protein per 100g. Volumes as tapered cylinders less about a quarter for bone give roughly 105g and 115g, so ABOUT 190g OF MEAT AND SKIN TOTAL…

Breakfast (cont.): one thick slice of her own homemade whole grain multi-seed bread, her words, baked as an attempt at Dulce Sol and reported by her as not looking like it yet. The crumb is visibly dense and tight with whole seeds distributed right through it rather than only on the crust. CARD AND BREAD LIE TOGETHER ON THE SAME PLACEMAT, WHICH IS THE GOOD GEOMETRY ESTABLISHED ON 2026-08-13 AND THE ARRANGEMENT TO KEEP ASKING FOR: same plane, same depth, so no plane-offset term and no perspective term across the frame, the two error sources that produced the 2x plum miss last night. MEASURED BY DIRECT RATIO RATHER THAN BY ABSOLUTE px/mm, WHICH IS THE ROBUST METHOD WHEN BOTH OBJECTS SHARE A PLANE AND A ROUGH ORIENTATION: whatever foreshortening applies, it applies to both nearly equally and divides out, so no viewing angle needs to be recovered at all. The card images with a long axis of about 379px and a short of about 209px, the slice at about 545px long and 274px wide, both with their long axes running roughly the same direction in frame. That gives a length ratio of 1.44 against the card's 85.6mm for A SLICE LENGTH OF ABOUT 123mm, and a width ratio of 1.31 against the card's 54.0mm for A SLICE WIDTH OF ABOUT 71mm. Thickness is the one weak term here because the shot is close to top-down at roughly 29 degrees off vertical, leaving little side profile; the visible crust edge reads about 16mm, and given that photo-inferred depth has read LOW three times in this log it is taken as 17mm with an honest range of 15 to 20mm. Face area about 87 square cm reduced to roughly 74 after allowing for the rounded taper, times 1.7cm, gives APPROXIMATELY 126ml. Density taken at 0.45 g/ml, appropriate to a dense homemade whole-grain seeded loaf and far above the 0.20 of airy commercial white, giving ABOUT 55g with a range of 45 to 65g. Macros at whole-grain multi-seed values of roughly 40g carbohydrate, 11g protein, 7g fiber and 275 calories per 100g, the seed and fat content pulli…

Breakfast: a bowl of plain homemade yogurt heaped with hemp hearts, whole cashews, chunks of red-skinned apple with the skin left on, and a scatter of black sesame seeds. PORTIONS TAKEN FROM THE STORED BOWL ANCHOR RATHER THAN FROM PHOTO DEPTH, WHICH IS THE CORRECTION LEARNED YESTERDAY: her yogurt bowl was established at approximately 220ml capacity on 2026-08-13 after I read it as 120ml from an image, so capacity is used here as the primary input and the photo only confirms it. That confirmation does hold — the SPG card lying on the placemat gives roughly 3.8 px/mm at the mat plane, the bowl rim images at about 478px across, and correcting for the rim sitting roughly 7cm above the mat and nearer the lens at an estimated 45cm distance gives an outer rim of about 106mm and an inner of about 95mm, which for a rounded bowl implies roughly 224ml. TWO INDEPENDENT ROUTES AGREEING AT 220 TO 225ml IS THE FIRST TIME THAT HAS HAPPENED IN THIS LOG. Note the geometry is still the weaker arrangement flagged on 2026-08-13: the card is on the placemat while the food is up in an elevated bowl, so they are NOT in the same plane, and the agreement above should be read as the stored anchor being confirmed rather than as the card having become reliable at different depths. Contents fill the bowl to the rim with a central mound, so about 220 to 250ml total, apportioned as approximately 140g of yogurt forming the base, a generous 25g or about two and a half tablespoons of hemp hearts in the central pile, 12g of whole cashews at roughly nine nuts counted directly off the image, about 70g of apple across the visible red-skinned chunks, and roughly 2g of black sesame. Hemp is the dominant macro contributor here despite its small volume, supplying nearly half the protein and a third of the calories at 31.6g protein and 553 calories per 100g. Yogurt taken as plain and unsweetened at 4.7g carbohydrate per 100g per her confirmed homemade preparation, never sweetened. ALSO IN FRAME AND DELIBERAT…

Dinner (evening fruit): one whole dark purple-red plum or pluot with pale speckling and skin intact, uncut, resting on a paper towel in low kitchen light. NO SPG CARD IN FRAME, so the scale reference is the AirPods Pro case lying beside it, and THIS IS A DELIBERATELY WEAKER REFERENCE THAN THE CARD AND THE ENTRY SHOULD BE READ THAT WAY: the case is a three-dimensional box at 60.6 by 45.2 by 21.7mm rather than a flat rectangle, so which face is presented and how much of the depth wall is visible are both ambiguous in this lighting, and unlike the card it cannot yield a viewing angle by aspect comparison. Taking the case's largest in-frame extent of about 290px as its 60.6mm long dimension gives roughly 4.8 px/mm. The plum images at about 362px across by 340px, near enough circular, WHICH IS THE ONE THING THAT MAKES THIS TRACTABLE: a sphere silhouettes as a circle from every angle, so unlike the lentil plate and the bread slice there is no depth-axis or thickness term to get wrong here, and today's three under-reads do not apply. Raw diameter is therefore about 73mm, but the plum is a ball sitting ON the towel with its centre roughly 35mm above the reference plane while the case sits flat, so the plane-offset correction at an estimated 30cm camera distance is 265 over 300 or 0.883, giving A CORRECTED DIAMETER OF ABOUT 65mm. Treating it as slightly oblate at 6.5 by 6.5 by 5.8cm gives approximately 128ml, so about 120g gross and roughly 115g of flesh once the pit is removed. THAT IS A LARGE PLUM, well above the USDA large at 66g, which is consistent with the deep colour and speckling of a pluot or Black Splendor rather than a supermarket red plum, but the honest range given the softer reference is 100 to 140g and the carb figure moves about 2g across it. Macros taken at pluot values of roughly 13g carbohydrate and 55 calories per 100g rather than common plum values, since the fruit reads as one of the sweeter dark cultivars. NOT CUMULATIVE: the previous food was the 18:…

Dinner (cont.): one hand-cut slice of rustic country bread with a thick seeded crust and an open crumb, eaten alongside the 18:41 lentils, the napkin showing stew-coloured stains that suggest she is mopping the plate with it. THIS IS THE CLEANEST CALIBRATION GEOMETRY THIS LOG HAS RECEIVED AND IT SHOULD BE THE TEMPLATE: the SPG card lies on the same napkin as the bread, so both sit in the SAME PLANE and NO PLANE-OFFSET CORRECTION IS NEEDED, which removes the 17 percent volume term that a card-on-table versus food-on-plate arrangement always carries.
